name: Gordon de Quetteville Robin
summary: Australian-British glaciologist who pioneered radio echo sounding for ice sheet measurement and directed SPRI 1958–1982.

name: David J. Drewry
summary: Glaciologist and author of this remembrance; succeeded Robin as SPRI director in 1984.

name: Stan Evans
summary: Physicist recruited by Robin to SPRI in 1959; co-pioneer of radio echo sounding technique.

name: Charles Swithinbank
summary: Glaciologist who worked with Robin on NBSE seismic survey and later SPRI airborne expeditions.

name: Peter Melleby
summary: Norwegian colleague who worked with Robin on NBSE seismic campaign preparation.

name: Mark Oliphant
summary: Physics professor at Birmingham University who supervised Robin's nuclear physics studies.

name: Raymond Priestley
summary: Geologist and vice-chancellor at Birmingham University who directed Robin to SPRI.

name: James Wordie
summary: SPRI figure who, via Priestley's recommendation, offered Robin the Signy Island position.

name: Peter Wadhams
summary: Robin's student and colleague at SPRI; later became SPRI director in 1987.

name: Terence Armstrong
summary: SPRI colleague who served as acting director after Robin's retirement; co-developed Diploma in Polar Studies.

name: Jean Robin
summary: Robin's wife, married 1953; formerly Lawrence Kirwan's secretary at Royal Geographical Society.

name: Caroline Robin
summary: Robin's daughter.

name: Elizabeth Robin
summary: Robin's daughter.

name: Jay Zwally
summary: NASA scientist who took up Robin's satellite altimetry ideas for polar ice sheet observation.

name: Geoffrey Hattersley-Smith
summary: Canadian Defence Research Board scientist who participated in 1966 Ellesmere Island airborne RES.

name: David Meldrum
summary: Robin's research student who commented on Robin's scientific acumen.

name: Fred Roots
summary: Commentator who noted Robin's role in making scientific cooperation a factor in Antarctic Treaty activities.

name: Lawrence Kirwan
summary: Royal Geographical Society figure for whom Jean Robin worked as secretary.

name: Larry Gould
summary: Officially opened the SPRI extension facility in 1968.

name: Scott Polar Research Institute
summary: Polar research institute at University of Cambridge; Robin served as director 1958–1982.

name: University of Cambridge
summary: British university where SPRI is based; awarded Robin ScD in 1977.

name: University of Melbourne
summary: Australian university where Robin read physics and gained Master's Degree in 1942.

name: Birmingham University
summary: British university where Robin studied nuclear physics under Oliphant and later held lectureship.

name: Wesley College
summary: Melbourne school where Robin was educated and became a Rover Scout.

name: Royal Australian Naval Voluntary Reserve
summary: Australian naval reserve force Robin joined upon graduating in 1942.

name: HMS Stygian
summary: British submarine Robin joined as lieutenant towards end of World War II.

name: Falkland Islands Dependencies Survey
summary: British Antarctic survey organization that employed Robin as base commander at Signy Island 1947–48.

name: Norwegian-British-Swedish Antarctic Expedition
summary: Antarctic expedition 1949–52 where Robin served as third-in-command and physicist in charge of seismic survey.

name: Australian National University
summary: Australian university where Robin briefly worked on ocean waves in early 1957.

name: Jodrell Bank Observatory
summary: Manchester observatory from which Stan Evans was recruited to SPRI in 1959.

name: Canadian Defence Research Board
summary: Canadian defense research organization; Geoffrey Hattersley-Smith participated in 1966 RES work.

name: US National Science Foundation
summary: US funding agency that collaborated with Robin on 12-year Antarctic ice sheet mapping programme 1967–79.

name: Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research
summary: International scientific organization coordinating Antarctic research; Robin was president 1970–74.

name: International Council of Scientific Unions
summary: International scientific body that created SCAR in 1958.

name: Royal Society
summary: UK scientific academy; formed British National Committee on Antarctic Research and appointed Robin as Permanent UK Delegate.

name: British National Committee on Antarctic Research
summary: UK committee formed by Royal Society; Robin served as Permanent UK Delegate until 1984.

name: Ford Foundation
summary: Philanthropic organization that provided substantial financial support for SPRI extension.

name: Darwin College
summary: Cambridge college where Robin was Fellow since founding in 1964; served as vice-master 1974–78.

name: British Antarctic Survey
summary: UK Antarctic research organization; Drewry departed for BAS in 1987.

name: Royal Geographical Society
summary: UK geographical society; awarded Robin Back Grant 1952 and Patron's Gold Medal 1979.

name: International Glaciological Society
summary: International society that awarded Robin the Seligman Crystal in 1986.

name: University of Stockholm
summary: Swedish university that awarded Robin honorary doctorate in 1978.

name: Royal Society of Edinburgh
summary: Scottish learned society that awarded Robin the Bruce Medal in 1953.

name: NASA
summary: US space agency that took up Robin's satellite altimetry ideas for polar ice sheet observation.

name: US Office of Naval Research
summary: US Navy research office that provided long-term funding for SPRI submarine profile analysis.

name: Royal Navy
summary: UK naval service that negotiated informal agreement with SPRI for Arctic submarine data collection in early 1970s.

name: Technical University of Denmark
summary: Danish university that participated in Robin's 1967–79 Antarctic mapping campaign.

name: Melbourne
summary: Australian city where Robin was born and educated.

name: Victoria
summary: Australian state whose mountains Robin hiked and skied in as a Rover Scout.

name: England
summary: Country Robin moved to during World War II for naval service.

name: English Channel
summary: Waterway where Robin spent a month on motor torpedo boats.

name: Jahore Straits
summary: Strait near Singapore where HMS Stygian supported midget submarine attack on Japanese cruisers.

name: Singapore harbour
summary: Harbour where HMS Stygian supported midget submarine attack.

name: Signy Island
summary: South Orkneys island where Robin served as FIDS base commander 1947–48.

name: Cape Geddes
summary: Location on Laurie Island where Robin first wintered in South Orkneys.

name: Laurie Island
summary: South Orkneys island with Argentine station; Robin wintered at Cape Geddes here.

name: Montevideo
summary: Uruguayan city from which Robin sailed to South Orkneys on SS Trepassey.

name: Maudheim
summary: NBSE station in Dronning Maud Land, Antarctica where Robin wintered 1949–52.

name: Dronning Maud Land
summary: Antarctic region where Maudheim station was located.

name: Weddell Sea
summary: Antarctic sea where Robin studied ocean wave penetration into sea ice 1959–60.

name: Greenland
summary: Arctic ice sheet where Robin conducted RES field work in 1964.

name: Ellesmere Island
summary: Canadian Arctic island where first continuous airborne RES was made in 1966.

name: Antarctic Peninsula
summary: Antarctic region where Swithinbank undertook first SPRI airborne season 1966–67.

name: Devon Island
summary: Canadian Arctic island where Robin spent spring 1973 on ice cap.

name: Ross Ice Shelf
summary: Antarctic ice shelf where Robin's RES work identified ice streams flowing into it.

name: Lake Vostok
summary: Large subglacial water body beneath East Antarctic Ice Sheet discovered through Robin's RES work.

name: East Antarctic Ice Sheet
summary: Antarctic ice sheet under which Lake Vostok lies.

name: Canada
summary: Country where Robin presented 1965 satellite altimetry paper at conference.

name: Cape Town
summary: South African city where Robin's 1993–94 Antarctic visit commenced.

name: Halley
summary: British Antarctic research station Robin visited during 1993–94 trip.

name: Cape Norvegia
summary: Antarctic cape near Maudheim that Robin glimpsed during 1993–94 visit.

name: Arctic
summary: Polar region where Robin negotiated Royal Navy submarine data collection in early 1970s.

name: Camp Century
summary: Greenland site where Robin and Evans conducted 1964 RES traverse.

name: SS Trepassey
summary: Ship on which Robin sailed from Montevideo to South Orkneys in 1947.

name: RSS John Biscoe
summary: Ship on which Robin conducted ocean wave study in Weddell Sea 1959–60.

name: DHC-3 Otter
summary: Aircraft used for first continuous airborne RES in Ellesmere Island 1966.

name: RSS Bransfield
summary: Ship on which Robin's 1993–94 Antarctic visit commenced from Cape Town.

name: HMS Endurance
summary: Royal Navy ship on which Robin traveled to Signy Island in 1993–94.

name: Weasels
summary: Tracked vehicles Robin and Melleby prepared for NBSE seismic campaign.

name: RES prototype 35 MHz
summary: Purpose-built radio echo sounding prototype operating at 35 MHz, first field-tested in Antarctica 1963.

name: Polar Medal
summary: British award given to Robin for NBSE scientific success 1950–52.

name: Norwegian Medal for Civil Services
summary: Norwegian award with clasp 'Maudheim' given to Robin for NBSE work.

name: Bruce Medal
summary: Royal Society of Edinburgh award given to Robin in 1953.

name: Back Grant
summary: Royal Geographical Society award given to Robin in 1952.

name: Patron's Gold Medal
summary: Royal Geographical Society award given to Robin in 1979.

name: Seligman Crystal
summary: International Glaciological Society's foremost prize awarded to Robin in 1986.

name: NBSE report 1958
summary: Publication of Robin's seismic traverse work, published as NBSE report in 1958.

name: Journal of Glaciology temperature paper
summary: Seminal paper by Robin on temperature distribution in moving ice sheets.

name: Philosophical Transactions 1963 paper
summary: Robin's 1963 paper on ocean wave decay in marginal ice zone.

name: Mapping the Antarctic ice sheet by satellite altimetry
summary: Key 1965 conference paper by Robin on satellite altimetry for polar ice sheets.

name: Diploma in Polar Studies
summary: Post-graduate qualification developed by Robin and Armstrong at SPRI, commenced intake October 1975.

name: MPhil in Polar Studies
summary: One-year master's degree that replaced Diploma in Polar Studies from 1980.

name: SPRI extension
summary: New SPRI facility with laboratories, library and archive space; opened officially 1968.
